native_result.query: What proportion of original studies in Experimental Economics were conducted in the United Kingdom?
native_result.HypoA: The original studies in Experimental Economics were primarily conducted in the United States (61.1%), while the replication studies were more distributed across countries like Austria (27.8%), Germany (11.1%), Singapore (27.8%), the United Kingdom (11.1%), and the United States (22.2%).
native_result.HypoB: About 5.6% (1 of 18, ~0.056) of original studies in Experimental Economics were conducted in the United Kingdom — a token share, versus 61% (11/18) conducted in the United States. This comes from counting experiment_country.o over all 18 unique original papers (title+authors.o+pub_year fingerprint, no exclusions) with project=='ee' in meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv; all 18 rows have a recorded country, so the known-country denominator is also 18, and the estimate is unchanged (0.00 pp) under unit choice (O/R rows vs unique studies), missing-drop, drop==True exclusion, or an expanded UK spelling list. Caveats: with n=18 a single study shifts the proportion by ~5.5 percentage points, so this is a coarse descriptive share rather than a precise population estimate, and recorded values were accepted at face value (e.g. ee.16 Kirchler et al. is recorded as 'Germany'), with no external correction. Definitions based on experiment_country.r (replication site; 2/18 = 11.11%) or on the same_country==1 flag (6/18 = 33.33%) were deliberately rejected because the question concerns the location of the ORIGINAL study.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Read both CSVs with pandas; verified shapes (927x57 and 143x15) and that file 2 has no country column. 2) Filtered file 1 to project=='ee' -> 18 rows. 3) Built original-paper fingerprint = lower/whitespace-normalised title + authors.o + pub_year; drop_duplicates left 18 rows (0 removed) = denominator; cross-checked against unique id and unique title (also 18). 4) Checked experiment_country.o completeness: 0 NaN, 0 blank -> known-country denominator also 18. 5) Flagged UK by normalised membership in {united kingdom, uk, u.k., great britain, britain, england, gb, wales, scotland, northern ireland}: numerator = 1 (ee.13). 6) Computed 1/18 = 0.055556 = 5.5556% and printed the country value-count distribution. 7) Ran computed sensitivity variants (rows vs unique studies; known-country-only denominator; drop==True exclusion; narrow UK list; expanded UK list) plus two explicitly rejected variants (experiment_country.r = 2/18; same_country==1 = 6/18), reporting deltas in percentage points. 8) Cross-checked the cohort against file 2 ('Experimental Economics' = 18 rows / 18 unique labels) by parsing first-author surname + year from file-2 labels and matching authors.o + pub_year in file 1: 18/18 bijection, zero mismatches, zero unmatched ee ids. 9) Saved raw stdout and a summary. No meta-regression, no statistical model, no external data used.
